problem_statement: Ovidius is a front-end-development editorial blog built on Astro and Tailwind CSS: a homepage with a hero, a featured article and a Latest Articles list, a paginated /blog index that lists the nine articles, individual article pages under /blog/<slug>, and About, Contact and Terms pages, all wrapped in a shared Header (logo plus a Home/Blog/About/Contact nav) and a shared Footer. The blog hosts its own reading tool: a 'Browse the desk' category filter that sits above the article feed. It is a labelled row of the desk's five standing beat chips (Performance, Careers, Frameworks, Workflow, Tailwind CSS) plus an All chip, and a live readout that reports how many of the nine articles are showing for the chosen beat, in the form 'Showing N of 9 . <Beat>'. The filter is promoted on both surfaces that list posts: the blog index (/blog/) and the homepage's Latest Articles area. Ship the Browse-the-desk filter so it (1) appears above the article feed on the blog index AND on the home page, (2) lays out its chip row responsively so no reading surface overflows horizontally on a 390px phone, (3) matches the Ovidius primary/slate editorial styling (dashed primary-accent pill chips keyed to the theme tokens) rather than an off-palette gray slab or an overlapping pile of cards, and (4) keeps the readout in sync so a reader who clicks the Frameworks chip sees the feed narrow to the three framework articles and the readout update to 'Showing 3 of 9 . Frameworks' — it must re-read the live matched set, not show a stale captured value. Keep the rest of the theme — navigation, existing content, the paginated blog, RSS, the Astro build — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'Browse the desk' category filter above the article feed so it renders on BOTH the blog index (/blog/) and the home page's Latest Articles area (a shared component, not a per-page copy).
The filter shows a 'Browse the desk' label, a chip row of All plus the five standing beats (Performance, Careers, Frameworks, Workflow, Tailwind CSS), and a live 'Showing N of 9 . <Beat>' readout.
The chip row must wrap responsively so no reading surface overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).

Style the filter in the Ovidius primary/slate editorial language (dashed primary-accent pill chips keyed to the theme tokens, a legible active chip), not an off-palette gray/dark slab and not a collapsed pile of overlapping article cards.

Wire the chip clicks so that clicking a beat (for example Frameworks) re-filters the feed to the matching articles AND re-syncs the readout to 'Showing N of 9 . <Beat>' (for example 'Showing 3 of 9 . Frameworks'); marking the chip active is not sufficient — the readout must re-read the live matched set, not a stale captured value.
Preserve navigation (Home/Blog/About/Contact), the footer, the paginated blog, the existing article/about/contact content, images and the Astro build with no console or network errors.
design_constraints: Implement the Browse-the-desk filter as a shared component so a single source of truth reaches the blog index and the home page; do not paste divergent copies per page or build a detached widget.
The chip row must use a fluid, wrapping layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile.

The filter must adopt the Ovidius theme tokens (the #02738f primary accent, slate text, dashed primary borders, rounded pill chips, an uppercase small-caps label, the same margins/padding and font family) so it reads as part of the blog; the active chip must be legible (high-contrast primary fill), and the filtered feed must stay a tidy article column, not a negative-margin pile.
Keep the readout in sync with the CURRENT filter selection after every click by recomputing the visible count from the matched set, so it can never go stale relative to the shown articles.
Do not remove or regress the navigation, existing article/about/contact content, the paginated blog, RSS or the Astro build.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the homepage hero, featured article and Latest Articles area across viewports, and carry the Browse-the-desk filter on the home page (D2 cross-page presence).

desktop_blog, mobile_blog and tablet_blog frame the Browse-the-desk filter and article feed on the blog index across viewports; the reference keeps 0 overflow and a tidy grid, the negative controls overflow on mobile and (for the bad leg) collapse into overlapping cards.
desktop_post, desktop_about, mobile_about and desktop_contact protect the existing article, About and Contact reading surfaces.

blog_filter_frameworks clicks the Frameworks beat chip on the blog index; the feed must narrow to the three framework articles and the readout must re-sync to 'Showing 3 of 9 . Frameworks' (the interaction terminal state).
The mobile blog state (mobile_blog) is the horizontal-overflow discriminator: the reference reports 0 overflow while the fixed-width negative controls overflow.

change_completion: The Browse-the-desk filter is present above the feed on BOTH the blog index and the home page (the shared component reaches both routes).

After clicking the Frameworks beat chip on the blog index, the feed narrows to the three framework articles and the readout re-syncs to 'Showing 3 of 9 . Frameworks' — the post-interaction terminal state changed from 'Showing 9 of 9 . All beats'.
design_consistency: The filter on the blog states matches the reference's primary/slate editorial styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), with a legible active chip and a tidy article feed, not an off-palette slab or an overlapping pile.
The filter adopts the Ovidius theme tokens and dashed-chip idiom so it reads as part of the blog across every surface.
responsive: No captured reading surface overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the chip row wraps.
desktop_blog and tablet_blog keep the filter and article feed readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: Navigation (Home/Blog/About/Contact), the footer and the paginated blog remain present and functional.
The existing article/about/contact content, images, RSS and the Astro build are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

metadata.design_goal: add the blog's own on-brand 'Browse the desk' category filter across the post-listing surfaces with a live count readout, while keeping the navigation, paginated blog and Astro build stable
metadata.source_repo_kind: Astro editorial blog theme with shared Header/Footer, a homepage hero and article list, a paginated blog index, article routes and About/Contact/Terms pages, using Tailwind CSS theme tokens and local images
metadata.selected_repo_reason: JustGoodUI/ovidius-astro-theme is a runnable Astro 5 + Tailwind 4 editorial blog; it builds to static output offline and hosts a natural experience-continuity add on the blog's OWN post-listing category filter spanning a mobile-overflow defect, cross-page presence, filtered-feed layout, and chip-click count wiring.

author_notes: slot_167 rebuilt to a genre-native L4 on the JustGoodUI Ovidius Astro editorial-blog theme. The lever is the blog's OWN post feed and its native 'Browse the desk' category filter (All plus five standing beats over the nine real front-end articles, with a live 'Showing N of 9 . <Beat>' readout), not a bolted-on metric rail. Each article carries a real category (Performance, Careers, Frameworks, Workflow, Tailwind CSS) added to the Astro content schema and frontmatter. The filter is hardened to fail four orthogonal acceptance gates in the bad solution. Lever 1 (D6 no_horizontal_overflow): the chip row uses a fixed-width non-wrapping track that overflows a 390px phone; the reference wraps it. Lever 2 (D2 dom_assertions, cross-page): the 'Browse the desk' filter must be promoted on both the blog index and the home page; reference promotes it on both, baseline and bad only on the blog index so both fail the home-page presence assertion. Lever 3 (D3 visual_regression): the bad filtered feed collapses — the article cards are pulled together with negative margins so they shingle into an illegible overlapping pile and the active chip is near-white text on a near-white fill — failing pixelmatch/ssim/block fidelity against the tidy reference. Lever 4 (D4 interaction_assertions): the bad chip click flips .is-active and hides cards but rewrites the readout from a label snapshotted in a closure, so after the Frameworks click the readout stays 'Showing 9 of 9 . All beats'. Four leg-varying files (src/components/PostFilter.astro, src/styles/deskfilter.css, src/pages/index.astro, src/pages/blog/[...page].astro) live in suggested_files; the article content, images and content schema category taxonomy are shared byte-identically across legs. Built offline as static Astro output served by a static file server, with the article images and Figtree fonts local and no network calls; that infrastructure is identical across legs.
